title.narrative: SECOND PHASE OF NATIONAL URBAN POLICY PROGRAMME

description.narrative:
Since 2017, a pilot phase of a National Urban Policy programme (NUPP) has been implemented, funded by MOLIT. The funding for pilot phase of the NUP programme will be end in 2022. Currently, UN-Habitat and MOLIT are in the process of renewing its partnership programme, hereby expanding and promoting desirable and people-centered smart cities in a rapidly urbanizing world.
This project aims to promote people-centered smart cities through national urban policies, and based on a collaboration with MOLIT, by strengthening capacities of policy makers in participating countries and building on the lessons learnt from the pilot phase of a National Urban Policy Programme which has been implemented.
Through the processes of developing the policies and strategies for people-centered smart cities, the second phase of the National Urban Policy Programme will endeavor to build capacity to develop, implement and monitor and evaluate urban policy in selected countries, implement the NUPs through demonstration projects identified using a smart city approach, and provide for knowledge creation, knowledge exchange on urban policy through an online platform and in person conferences and workshops.
UN-Habitat focuses its work on the promotion and adoption of improved policies, plans, instruments and processes that lead to more compact, socially inclusive, better integrated and connected cities and territories, that promote sustainable urban development and are resilient to climate change. Equally, one of its key flagship programme promotes the deployment of technological innovations to realize sustainability, inclusivity, prosperity and human rights. This will make the urban digital transformation work for the benefit of all. There is an urgent need for building inclusive and transformative digital capacity of local and national authorities on digital transitions in urbanization. Moreover, this programme will contribute to the enhanced investment opportunities for smart cities and augmented capacity of government of all levels to adopt people-centered smart city approaches aiming at the contribution to implementing the 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda as well as the New Urban Agenda.
Main expected accomplishment are as below; Outcome 1: National and local governments mainstream the people-centered smart cities approach into NUPs and / or sub-national urban policies in selected countries and sub-national regions. Outcome 2: Capacity of policy makers and stakeholders enhanced to facilitate the territorial dimension of urban innovation and steer digital transformation in NUPs / SUPs. Outcome 3: Urban/metropolitan interventions apply innovative approaches and technologies while considering the people-centered dimension in National Urban Policy. Outcome 4: Improved knowledge creation and sharing, and enhanced global awareness of experiences on the nexus of NUP and people-centered smart cities approaches and models.
